name: C2b1a1c (Turkic branch)
description: C2b1a1c is the subclade of the Star Cluster dispersed into Turkic-speaking populations through the administrative, military, and political structures of the Mongol Empire and its successor states. As the Mongol Empire fragmented into the Golden Horde, Chagatai Khanate, and Ilkhanate, C2b1a1-bearing men integrated into local Turkic-speaking populations across Central Asia, the Kazakh steppe, Uzbekistan, and the Uyghur territories of western China. Over the following centuries, many of these lineages were absorbed into Turkic ethnic identities while retaining their Mongolic paternal DNA. The relatively recent MRCA (~1,200 CE) closely matches the peak of Mongol imperial expansion, supporting the historical model of gene flow through military and administrative contact.
interestingFact: C2b1a1c is a genetic trace of the political assimilation of Mongol lineages into Turkic cultures — men whose Y chromosomes mark them as patrilineal descendants of the Mongol expansion, yet whose descendants speak Turkic languages and identify as Kazakh, Uzbek, or Uyghur, illustrating how genetic and cultural identity can diverge over just a few generations.

clans.name: Golden Horde
clans.note: Western successor state of the Mongol Empire; Chinggisid lineages entered Kazakh and Bashkir gene pools through the Golden Horde administrative class

clans.name: Chagatai Khanate
clans.note: Central Asian successor state governing Transoxiana and Xinjiang; C2b1a1c carriers integrated into the Uzbek and Uyghur populations of this region

clans.name: Kerei (Kazakh)
clans.note: Large Kazakh clan with significant Mongol-era ancestry reflected in C2b1a1c frequency
